name: One-time code input
summary: A verification code field drawn as a row of boxes, one per digit.
description:
Use it for two-step sign-in, email and phone verification codes.

It is one real <input> in a .v-otp wrapper, not six separate fields, so pasting a code, SMS autofill on phones, password managers and screen readers all work as with any field, and it needs no JS. The wrapper draws a box per digit and the digits are spaced to sit in them. Set --v-otp-length to the code's length and match maxlength and pattern.

classes.name: v-otp
classes.description: The wrapper that draws the boxes. --v-otp-length sets how many (default 6); --v-otp-cell and --v-otp-gap their size.

classes.name: v-otp-input
classes.description: The input inside. Give it autocomplete="one-time-code", inputmode="numeric", maxlength and a pattern.

states.description: Lets phones offer the code from a text message and password managers fill it.
Such as [0-9]{6}. A code that does not match marks the boxes in the danger colour after the person has typed (:user-invalid).
The code length, so a seventh digit cannot be typed.

keyboard.action: Types a digit into the next box. Backspace, arrow keys and paste work as in any text field.

a11y: One field means one label and one announcement, not six fields called "digit 1" to "digit 6".
Pasting the whole code works because it is a single field; nothing has to spread it across boxes.
Link the hint ("We sent a 6-digit code to your phone") with aria-describedby.

examples.title: Six-digit code
examples.description: Type, paste or let the phone fill it.
examples.html: We sent a 6-digit code to your phone.
